name: Stapleton postcoital prophylaxis
question: Does postcoital trimethoprim–sulfamethoxazole prevent recurrent urinary tract infection compared with postcoital placebo in healthy young women?

design.population: Healthy young women prone to recurrent urinary tract infections.

verdictNote: Small trial; the abstract does not identify a prespecified primary endpoint or threshold.
takeaway: In healthy young women with recurrent urinary tract infections, postcoital trimethoprim–sulfamethoxazole reduced recurrence compared with postcoital placebo over more than six months: 2/16 versus 9/11 women developed infection.

reports.label: Primary report
reports.citation: Stapleton A, Latham RH, Johnson C, et al. "Postcoital antimicrobial prophylaxis for recurrent urinary tract infection. A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial." *JAMA.* 1990;264(6):703-706. doi:10.1001/jama.1990.03450060049027
reports.followUp: More than six months of observation

results.measure: Women with at least one UTI during more than six months of observation
results.note: The abstract does not identify a prespecified primary endpoint, statistical test or threshold.

results.measure: Infections per patient-year during more than six months of observation
